faqs.a: JSX is the syntax React uses for markup. Browsers understand SVG attributes like class and stroke-width, but React expects className and strokeWidth. This tool applies every rename and conversion for you.
faqs.q: Why can't I paste SVG directly into React?

faqs.a: The tool checks that your code parses as XML with a single <svg> root. Common causes of the error: unclosed tags, an unescaped & in a path, or pasting HTML instead of SVG.

svg-to-jsx-converter.formula:
Attribute renames:
class → className, for → htmlFor
stroke-width → strokeWidth (hyphenated names become camelCase)
data-* and aria-* stay unchanged
xlink:href → xlinkHref

Style strings become objects:
style="font-size:14px;fill:red" → style={{ fontSize: '14px', fill: 'red' }}

Empty elements self-close: <circle … />
Root gets {...props} when the spread option is on.

keyFacts: JSX looks like HTML but is JavaScript: React requires camelCase attributes (strokeWidth, not stroke-width) and className instead of class.
The converter parses your SVG as real XML with the browser's DOMParser — malformed markup is reported, never silently mangled.
Every element is counted and re-serialised with consistent 2-space indentation, so the output is readable and diff-friendly.
Text like {braces} inside SVG text nodes is escaped to {'{'} so it renders literally instead of breaking your component.
The preview panel renders your original SVG with scripts and event handlers stripped for safety.

limitations: The tool converts markup only — it does not rewrite your component logic or CSS.
External references (use href to another file, external images) still need those files at runtime.
Very large SVGs (hundreds of elements) convert fine but produce long files; consider SVGR-style optimisation for huge illustrations.
Animations defined with SMIL <animate> tags are copied as-is; React does not control them.

svg-to-jsx-converter.workedExample:
Input:
<svg width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24">
  <circle class="dot" cx="12" cy="12" r="10" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/>
  <text style="font-size:14px;fill:red">Hi</text>
</svg>

Output (bare JSX):
<svg width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24">
  <circle className="dot" cx="12" cy="12" r="10" strokeWidth="2" fill="none" />
  <text style={{ fontSize: '14px', fill: 'red' }}>Hi</text>
</svg>

What changed: class → className, stroke-width → strokeWidth, the style string became a style object, the empty circle self-closed, and the text stayed inline.
